We read in Habakkuk: "God will come from the south, and the Holy One from the shady mountain." "God will come from the south." It is said of the Savior: because God was born in the south. For by the situation of Jerusalem, Bethlehem is set to the south: therefore it is said, "God will come from the south." But if "God will come from the south," how is it now said, "From the rising of the sun and from its setting, from the north"? The south wind, the auster and the notus, is passed over in silence.

3:4: ON THE EPIPHANY AND PSALM 28, HOMILY 89

What does the psalm have to say of the Savior? "As the beloved Son of unicorns." Our beloved Lord and Savior is the Son of the unicorns, the Son of the cross, of whom Habakkuk sings, "Rays shine forth from beside him, where his power is concealed." After this beloved Son was crucified, then, was fulfilled the prophecy of the psalm: "The voice of the Lord strikes fiery flames." For when Christ had been baptized and the entire universe had been purified in his cleansing, the fire of hell was extinguished.
